Action Plan:
1. Book face-to-face GP clinic appointment within the next 4–5 days for otoscopic examination of the left ear to exclude cerumen impaction or other external/middle-ear pathology.  Patient to telephone support team (number provided in notes) to secure a slot; admin team alerted via internal message.
2. Provide patient-education leaflet on tinnitus (link pasted into consultation notes) for review prior to clinic visit.
3. Advise patient to monitor hearing, tinnitus, and balance; if symptoms worsen or new features develop (e.g., severe vertigo, pain, discharge), arrange an urgent video or in-person review.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 32-year-old male (Jack Smith, DOB 31 Oct 1990).  
• Presenting complaint: progressive, intermittent difficulty hearing in the left ear for ~6 weeks.  
   – Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in the left ear; masking effect with TV/music.  
   – Occasional mild light-headedness/“off-balance” sensation; no true spinning vertigo; no nausea.  
• No ear pain, discharge, itching, fever, chest pain or palpitations.  
• Similar but brief (2-day) episode of hearing difficulty ~1 year ago.  
• Denies cotton-bud use.  
Past Medical/Surgical History: none reported other than brief prior hearing episode.  
Medications: none reported.  
Allergies: not discussed.  
Social history: not discussed (noise exposure, smoking, alcohol not covered).

Objective:
• No physical examination performed in video consult.  
• No vital signs or investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Issue: Left-ear hearing loss  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Cerumen impaction causing conductive hearing loss (DDx rank: “Cerumen impaction” – High likelihood).  
   – Differential diagnoses:  
     • Menière’s disease (Medium).  
     • Serous otitis media / Eustachian-tube dysfunction (Medium).  
     • Acoustic neuroma (Low–Medium).  
     • Viral labyrinthitis/neuritis (Low).  
   – Investigations planned: Otoscopic examination at upcoming clinic visit (± audiometry depending on findings).  
   – Treatment planned: If wax present, ear syringing or microsuction per clinic protocol.  
   – Referral: None at this stage; consider ENT/audiology if hearing loss persists or non-wax pathology found.

2. Issue: Tinnitus (left ear)  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Tinnitus secondary to underlying ear pathology (see Issue 1).  
   – Differential diagnoses: As above.  
   – Investigations planned: Same otoscopic exam; further audiology/ENT work-up if persists after initial management.  
   – Treatment planned: Education leaflet on tinnitus; reassurance; discuss masking strategies.  
   – Referral: Consider ENT if persistent after ear pathology ruled out.

3. Issue: Intermittent light-headedness / disequilibrium  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Mild vestibular disturbance likely related to ear condition.  
   – Differential diagnoses: Menière’s disease; viral labyrinthitis; acoustic neuroma (low likelihood given short duration).  
   – Investigations planned: None immediately; will reassess after ear examination.  
   – Treatment planned: Observation; safety advice.  
   – Referral: ENT if balance symptoms worsen or persist.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: allergies, current medications, occupational/social noise exposure, family ENT history not elicited.  
• Transcript vs. DDx conflicts: none identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise.
